text.brief: In January 1993 Jiang Zemin told the Central Military Commission that the army must prepare to win local wars under high-technology conditions.
text.record: Coalition forces had broken Iraq's army in 1991 after six weeks of air war and a hundred hours on the ground. Party military journals spent the years after on precision strike, satellites and battlefield networks. The 1993 guidelines made local war under high-technology conditions the basis for planning. A 2004 revision changed the phrase to informatized conditions, and later defense white papers kept it.
text.reading: The Party watched an American victory from across the river, which is Stratagem 9, and learned from it faster than the victors did. The lesson it drew was asymmetry, so it built missiles, satellites and cyber units to strike the networks that made American precision possible.
text.gapText: Architecture Principles. The United States showed its method to the world and assumed its lead would hold.
text.fix: Design every American advantage on the assumption that the opponent studies it, and harden the networks it depends on first.
